fields.acceptance: A testscript runs rhiza root init, then rhiza root show --json from the root, from a registered project and from a <project>.<slug> sibling worktree, and gets the same root each time; a second root init on the same directory exits 2 with a next.
fields.statement: rhiza root init [dir] makes a directory a Rhiza root by writing <dir>/rhiza.toml (its projects and machine-wide settings), and every rhiza command finds its root by walking up from the working directory to the nearest rhiza.toml.

fields.acceptance: Testscript cases in the root-init script cover the root, a project, a sibling worktree, the root itself (no project) and a directory outside any root (exit 2, next names root init).
fields.statement: rhiza root show [--json] prints the root, its config file and the project the working directory belongs to (by its folder or a <project>.<slug> sibling worktree), or none at the root itself; outside any root it exits 2 with next rhiza root init.

fields.acceptance: A testscript adds a checkout and sees it in rhiza.toml and in rhiza project ls --json, and gets exit 2 for a path outside the root, a nested path, a non-git folder and a duplicate name.
fields.statement: rhiza project add <path> registers an existing git checkout that sits directly under the root, named by its folder (or --name), recording its repo ID when it has .rhiza/; a path outside the root or nested deeper, a non-git folder and a taken name are refused with exit 2 and a next.

fields.acceptance: A testscript adds a local bare repo by its file:// URL (no network) and finds the clone under the root and in project ls; a bad URL exits non-zero and leaves rhiza.toml unchanged.
fields.statement: rhiza project add <git URL> clones the repo into <root>/<name> (name from the URL or --name) and registers it as project add <path> does; a failed clone registers nothing.

fields.acceptance: A testscript registers one initialised and one bare git checkout, sees initialised and not initialised in project ls --json, removes one with project rm and finds its folder still on disk.
fields.statement: rhiza project ls [--json] lists each registered project with its name, path, repo ID and whether it is initialised (has .rhiza/) or not initialised; rhiza project rm <name> unregisters a project without touching its files.

fields.acceptance: A testscript gets exit 2 with the next from rhiza request in an unregistered repo and in a repo under no root, and runs rhiza check there successfully.
fields.statement: Starting a run or queuing a request (rhiza run start, rhiza request) needs a registered project under a root and otherwise exits 2 with a next naming rhiza root init or rhiza project add; model commands (show, apply, check, render, land) keep working in any repo with .rhiza/, so CI needs no root.
